---
title: "Could we solve this faster with AeroSandbox's own tools?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
# Geometry, ballast and the whole trajectory in one Opti, with the aerodynamics
# traced into it symbolically rather than sampled onto a grid. Several starts,
# because one solve lands in whichever basin it started nearest.
f = optimise_flight(n=40)

assert f["Cm_residual"] < 1e-6           # trimmed at every node, not just claimed
assert f["static_margin"] >= SM_FLOOR - 1e-6
assert np.max(f["alpha"]) < CLEAN_ALPHA  # never stalls, within this model
assert f["n_converged"] >= 2             # enough starts landed to see a spread
assert f["spread"] > 0.01                # local optima, not one global answer
```

::: {.hero}
[`{python} f"{f['duration']:.2f}"` s]{.hero-value}
[best of `{python} f"{f['n_converged']}"` local optima, at `{python} f"{len(f['t'])}"` nodes]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** Yes: `dyn.op_point` feeds the state to `AeroBuildup`, collocation
states the flight as constraints, and IPOPT differentiates through it — the
surrogate goes, with its interpolation error and the CG mismatch it invited. But
IPOPT is a *local* optimiser and this space is not convex, so the speed must be
spent on starts: `{python} f"{f['n_converged']}"` converge, to optima up to
[`{python} f"{f['spread']:.1f}"` s apart]{.key}. More starts can only raise it.

::: {.callout-warning}
## It cannot loop
A point mass has no pitch state, so it never sees the launch transient.
:::

## Assumed

1. Point mass: attitude follows trim instantly.
2. **Trimmed at every node**, so α is the airframe's.
3. `{python} f"{len(FLIGHT_STARTS)}"` starts at `{python} f"{len(f['t'])}"` nodes.
4. **Not grid-converged**: 60 nodes gives 8% less.
